dish: Margherita / coal-fired New Yorker
w: 13-time World Pizza Champion Tony Gemignani's flagship; ranked #3 pizza in the U.S. by 50 Top Pizza. 12 styles cooked in seven ovens — the Neapolitan Margherita (limited daily) and the coal-fired New Yorker are the ones to get.

dish: Focaccia-crust square slice (clam & garlic)
w: Punk-rock North Beach institution since 1978; airy focaccia squares with an impeccably crunchy bottom, sold by the slice. The clam & garlic and the sausage combo are the classics — line out the door, takeout only.

dish: Molinari salami sandwich on Dutch crunch
w: Gold-medal Italian deli since 1896, one of the oldest in the U.S. House-cured Molinari salami piled on Dutch-crunch — a legendary counter sandwich by Washington Square.

dish: Joe's Special (ground beef, spinach, egg)
w: Family-run since 1937, overlooking Washington Square. The originator of the Joe's Special — a mayor-proclaimed San Francisco classic — plus reliable red-sauce pasta and steaks in an old-school room.

dish: Tosca meatballs; house 'cappuccino'
w: Iconic 1919 North Beach bar-restaurant revived by Anna Weinberg, chef Nancy Oakes and Ken Fulk. Go for the scene, the Tosca meatballs, and the boozy house 'cappuccino' (armagnac and bourbon, no espresso).

dish: Neapolitan broccoli & salsiccia pizza; imported burrata
w: VPN-certified wood-fired Neapolitan pies (Caputo flour, DOP San Marzano) plus a mozzarella bar of imported bufala and burrata. Time Out rates it 5/5; the broccoli & salsiccia is the pick.

dish: Family-recipe house pastas, family-style
w: A North Beach red-sauce holdout tracing to 1906 (celebrated its 110th year in 2016). Old-school family-recipe pastas and a convivial, checkered-tablecloth room on Green St.

dish: Glazed oysters with lettuce cream; herb-crusted lamb
address: 800 North Point St, San Francisco, CA 94109
w: Michelin-starred SF institution since 1999 near the Wharf. Build a multi-course tasting around signatures like glazed oysters with lettuce cream and osetra, and herb-crusted loin of lamb.

dish: Sauerkraut pancakes; quail (the 'state bird')
w: James Beard Best New Restaurant (2013) and Michelin-starred. Dim-sum-style carts roll New American small plates — the namesake quail and the cheesy sauerkraut pancakes are essential.

dish: Mulhwe; uni-scallop toast; lime-soy fried chicken
w: Michelin Bib Gourmand (2023) — a contemporary Korean sharing-menu that folds in parmesan and chorizo alongside classics like mulhwe (raw seafood in chilled fermented-chili broth) and crackling lime-soy fried chicken.

dish: Wood-oven roast chicken for two with bread salad
w: James Beard Outstanding Restaurant winner and Michelin-listed; Judy Rodgers' brick-oven roast chicken for two over warm bread salad has been the city's defining Cal-cuisine dish since 1979.

dish: Wood-fired pork chop; wood-baked beans
w: The Divisadero gathering place that named a neighborhood; organic wood-fired California cooking whose pork chop is routinely called the best in the city, with bubbling wood-baked beans alongside.

dish: Sardine chips with horseradish crème fraîche
w: Hayes Valley's inventive Californian star (former Michelin star; #3 on the SF Chronicle Top 100, 2025). The sardine-threaded potato chips with horseradish dip are the signature opener.

dish: Seasonal tasting menu; dry-aged squab with mole
w: Chef Kim Alter's intimate Hayes Valley tasting-menu room behind a carved-owl door; a tightly orchestrated seasonal menu (dry-aged squab with cabbage and mole) with the Linden Room bar next door.

dish: Sesame-curry fried chicken; oysters; brunch under the films
w: James Beard-nominated Gayle Pirie and John Clark's California-Mediterranean landmark since 1999; oysters and sesame-curry fried chicken, with foreign films projected on the patio wall at dusk.

dish: Daily market menu; chilled squash soup
w: Melissa Perello's Michelin-recognized Castro bistro since 2010 — a refined but neighborly French-leaning California menu that changes daily; the closest clean fill for the French gap now that the classic French rooms have shuttered.

dish: Salted caramel ice cream
w: The Mission's iconic hand-churned creamery by Dolores Park (since 2006); the salted-caramel and coffee-toffee ice-cream sandwiches draw a line around the block.

dish: Malai kofta; blue-cheese naan; charred eggplant
w: James Beard-nominated Heena Patel's regional Gujarati cooking inside the Minnesota Street Project in Dogpatch; California-inflected home dishes like malai kofta, blue-cheese naan and fire-charred eggplant with garlic confit.

dish: Basteeya (phyllo-wrapped chicken & almond pie)
w: Mourad Lahlou's Richmond restaurant — the first Moroccan restaurant in the U.S. to earn a Michelin star (2010) — reimagining Moroccan cooking with California produce; the golden basteeya is the icon.

dish: Squab tacos on sourdough tortillas; Dungeness-crab tostada
w: Val Cantu's SoMa tasting-menu room — the world's first three-Michelin-star Mexican restaurant — fusing regional technique with Bay Area produce; squab tacos on house sourdough tortillas and a blue-masa Dungeness-crab tostada.

dish: Grilled lamb chops; moussaka; wood-grilled octopus
w: The city's definitive upscale Greek room in Jackson Square — open-hearth grill and wood oven perfuming a fireplace-lit dining room; grilled lamb chops, moussaka and some of the best grilled octopus in town.

dish: Embered oysters with smoked chili butter; radicchio salad
w: Michelin-starred, live-fire seafood from Saison Hospitality on the Embarcadero waterfront; embered oysters with smoked chili butter and a steak-knife radicchio salad, cooked over an open hearth.

dish: Pasta with faux foie gras & truffle; seasonal risotto
w: Suzette Gresham's two-Michelin-star Italian fine-dining room in a converted chapel on Nob Hill; house-made pastas, seasonal truffle risotto, and the signature ridged pasta with faux foie gras and truffle.

dish: Chicken-gizzard sisig pandesal; dry-aged duck 'adobo'
w: Michelin Bib Gourmand — the Bay Area's modern Filipino tasting-menu counter from chef Patrick Gabon; fermentation-driven takes like braised-gizzard sisig on brioche pandesal and dry-aged duck-breast adobo, 10-12 seats at a single counter.

dish: Old-fashioned scoops (100+ flavors)
w: The original Swensen's, opened 1948 at Hyde & Union on the Russian Hill cable-car line and the last U.S. parlor of the name — over 100 flavors churned old-school on the corner.
